newsitem.title: FRANCE: Colombia offers experience, help in Lima siege.
newsitem.headline: Colombia offers experience, help in Lima siege.

text.p: Colombia, which peacefully ended a similar attack 16 years ago, offered help on Wednesday in settling the guerrilla siege of the Japanese envoy's residence in Lima.

Colombian Foreign Minister Emma Maria Mejia, on a visit to Paris, said she did not know whether the Colombian ambassador was among at least 200 hostages held by heavily-armed guerrillas of the Cuban-inspired Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).
"This is very serious...I believe that of course we could cooperate if it were necessary but we trust Peru can solve this problem," she told Reuters.
Castroist M-19 guerrillas seized 14 ambassadors during a party at the Dominican embassy in Bogota in 1980 to demand the release of more than 300 jailed colleagues.
The siege lasted for more than two months and ended without bloodshed when the guerrillas dropped their demands, flew to Havana and released their hostages.
